answers.answer: Separate Conflict cards by I/II/III backs. Shuffle all four III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five on top of those; shuffle the three I cards and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck with 1 I, 5 II, and 4 III. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: Both human setups have two Agents on the Leader and a third Agent (the Swordmaster) next to the board; three troops in their garrison; and 1 water. In a four-player game the starting score is 1 VP; in a three-player game it is 0 VP.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker on ‘the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; place three troops in a garrison; take 1 water. Place two Agents on the Leader and the third next to the board.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents, but after taking it you are skipped for the rest of that phase and cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you, from Agent and Reveal turns, go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and after it ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal Effects use ‘just-revealed cards only’; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to your discard pile.

answers.answer: No. You must pay destination costs immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the card played, so that card's Agent-box effect cannot first provide resources to pay the entry cost. One Agent card can send only one Agent, using only one of its Agent icons. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can only be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs must be paid ‘before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; a card with no Agent icons ‘may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited that turn can deploy, plus up to two troops from the garrison. Thus, of the four already garrisoned, at most two can deploy (for up to five total if all three new troops deploy). At a non-Combat space, no troops deploy; recruited troops go to the garrison. Recruitment takes a troop from your supply and places it in your garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: a cube recruits a troop ‘from your supply’ into your garrison; at a Combat space, deploy any or all recruited this turn ‘plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; the Spy stays there. Infiltrate lets you recall your Spy from a post connected to a space occupied by another player's Agent, allowing your Agent to use that same space. Gather Intelligence lets you recall a Spy from a connected post whenever you send an Agent, to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving space or Agent-card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement, though two different Spies may be recalled for the two effects. The Spy Agent icon itself is an alternative icon for placement, not a recall.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon lets you use a connected space ‘you do not recall the Spy for this’; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; ‘You cannot recall the same Spy to both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.’

answers.answer: The total is 11 strength: two troops are 4, one sandworm is 3, and four revealed swords are 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0 regardless of revealed swords. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in Combat Intrigue; that window is for each player with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop is 2, each sandworm 3, and each revealed sword 1; you must have ‘at least one unit in the Conflict’ or strength is 0. Combat phase allows Combat Intrigue for players with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from playing later in the Combat Intrigue phase. The window closes once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, after which Combat resolves. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase’; resolve after players pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to supply and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: For a tie for first in a four-player game, both tied players take the second reward; neither wins or takes the Conflict card. The remaining players compete for the third reward only if exactly two tied for first; if three or more tied, there are no further rewards. In a three-player game, both tied players again take the second reward, neither takes the Conflict card, and no other rewards are given. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied for first each gain the second reward and ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; in three or fewer players no other rewards; in four, exactly two tied leaves the third reward for others. Resolve Combat says a player with 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards you take; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the 3-spice cost a second time to gain a second VP (6 spice total for 2 VP) when the reward is doubled.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘if you have one or more sandworms ... double the rewards’; control and battle icons cannot double. The example says a doubled reward may allow paying ‘6 spice to gain 2’ VP.

answers.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card into your supply, check whether you have another face-up Conflict or Objective card with the same battle icon. The matching pair must be flipped face down and scores 1 VP, so the match is mandatory. During Endgame, a wild battle icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair face down for 1 VP. The summary does not list a broader set of qualifying cards beyond face-up Conflict and Objective cards.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: after taking the won card, check for another ‘face-up Conflict or Objective card’ with the same icon; if so, you ‘must’ flip the pair. At Endgame, wild may match any of the three icons.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence with a Faction, gain 1 VP; that VP is lost if Influence drops below 2. At 4 Influence, gain the track-space bonus, which is kept even if Influence later drops below 4 (and can be earned again after dropping and re-advancing). The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance token and its VP. Merely tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not transfer it: the holder gives it up only when an opponent rises to a higher space. The FAQ also says a formerly tied player can take the Alliance if the holder later loses Influence after being tied.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: reaching 2 gives 1 VP, lost below 2; reaching 4 gives a bonus that is not given back; first to 4 takes the Alliance. It passes if an opponent rises to a ‘higher’ space. FAQ clarifies loss after a tie.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent during the Reveal turn before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split Persuasion from one source across different cards. After buying a Row card, its replacement is drawn immediately and may also be bought if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile; it is not used immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal Effects: Persuasion may be used ‘before, between, or after’ Reveal effects. Acquiring Cards says Persuasion can be pooled or split; replacement is drawn so ‘you may acquire its replacement’; acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.

answers.answer: In the Makers phase, put 1 bonus spice on each Maker space with no Agent; bonus spice accumulates, and visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there (along with the space's other effects). A Maker Hooks icon lets you take a token from the bank if you do not already have one; a Maker Hooks token is a requirement for sandworm summoning where the icon specifies it. The Shield Wall protects Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin Conflicts from sandworms while it remains; removing it allows sandworms at any Conflict. To summon, take a sandworm from the bank and immediately place it in your quadrant of the Conflict; a sandworm can never go in a garrison. A Shield Wall-protected Conflict blocks summoning.
answers.evidence: Makers: empty Maker spaces gain 1 spice and a visiting Agent gains ‘all the bonus spice there.’ Sandworms: summon and immediately deploy from bank to your Conflict quadrant; never in a garrison. Shield Wall lists its protected locations and removal effect.

answers.answer: The Endgame is triggered at Recall, at the end of a round, if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Before comparing scores, players may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards. The resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops. The FAQ adds that if all four resource tiebreakers are still tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins.
answers.evidence: Recall checks for Endgame. Scoring says at the end of a round trigger Endgame, then resolve Endgame Intrigue before winner comparison; tiebreaks are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops. FAQ gives the further Reveal-turn tiebreak.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup uses 20 contracts: shuffle them, place two face up on the board, and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and four Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left in the box for standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup: shuffle ‘20 contracts,’ flip two face up and place ‘the remaining 18 face down’; shuffle 4 additional cards into each deck. Shaddam is optional. Contrasting-back 10 are a separate Rise of Ix set, left out.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts, then replace it from the bank face up. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the contract's specified amount of spice that turn in total, including spice from other sources. The Immediate contract is completed as soon as taken. An Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract is completed when you next acquire that card. Completing any contract means announce it, gain its rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply. For a space contract, you must have held it when sending your Agent to that space.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: contract icon takes a face-up contract and replaces it; with none available it reverts to 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire timing, and says announce, take rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its printed rewards, then flip the token face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM: if you take a contract for a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ wait until a future turn and must have held the contract when sending. Completion: announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival receives the Ornithopter Objective. First Player goes to the human whose Objective shows the First Player marker; First Player alternates only between the humans. Each round the Rival acts immediately clockwise from First Player, so order is First Player → Rival → other human. A Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; give it the Ornithopter Objective; First Player alternates only between humans; turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. Agent turns: Rival ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: When a Rival reveals a card indicating an occupied board space, it ignores that destination and reveals another Hagal card until it can place an Agent on an unoccupied indicated space. A Place Spy card places a Spy on an empty post of its specified type, or ignores the placement if none is available; because it has not sent an Agent, it then reveals another Hagal card. Normal space costs and effects are ignored: apply only the Hagal card effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; ignore normal space costs/effects. Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty specified post or ignores placement and reveals another card. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
